source.title_on_document: Personalized AI Scaffolds Synergistic Multi-Turn Collaboration in Creative Work

supplement.where: Supplementary Materials appended to the PDF (PDF pp. 29-62, numbered 1-34). Data and code in an OSF repository titled 'CreativityBot: A Personalized AI Assistant to Support Creativity' (no URL printed in the text).
supplement.holds: Table S2 (arm sizes and demographics), Table S3 (quality regressions with SEs for GPT-4o-mini, small-LLM and large-LLM judges), Table S4 (alternative evaluation prompts), Fig. S2 (LLM Elo ratings and creativity by Elo tertile), the human expert validation (suppl. pp. 3-5), and all system prompts. All are in this PDF.

paper_design_summary: 331 U.S. Prolific workers with experience in marketing, design, or product management completed psychometric tests and an AI-led interview, then wrote a 300-400-word marketing campaign for a fictional lab-grown-meat startup with a GPT-4o chat assistant. They were randomized to a generic assistant, a fully personalized assistant (prompt includes their own psychological profile and interview summary), or a partially personalized assistant (prompt includes another participant's profile); there was no no-AI arm. Campaigns were scored for quality by an LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini, 1-10 rubric) and for creativity by an embedding measure of each campaign's distance from the average campaign; 100 AI-only simulated campaigns served as a further comparison.

studies.label: Marketing-campaign experiment (generic vs personalized vs partially personalized GPT-4o assistant)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Configuration of the GPT-4o assistant used to write the campaign: generic, fully personalized (own profile), or partially personalized (another participant's profile)
assignment.quote: We randomized 331 participants to work with AI that was either generic, partially personalized, or fully personalized.
assignment.locator: p. 1, Abstract; p. 8, Fig. 1 caption; p. 22, Experimental Design (partial personalization: 'we randomly assigned a subset of participants (n = 101)')
assignment.prereg_locator: p. 19, Participants: 'We re-registered our study design and primary analyses (OSF | CreativityBot: A Personalized AI Assistant to Support Creativity).' The document says 're-registered'; no registration date or listed primary outcome is printed.

arms.name: Generic AI
arms.description: GPT-4o (temperature 1) assistant prompted to ask focused questions, build on the person's contributions, and give feedback; given company description and initial campaign idea; no personal information

arms.name: Personalized AI
arms.description: Same prompt plus a GPT-4o summary of the participant's own psychological and creativity profile and a summary of their AI-guided interview on marketing experience and work style

arms.name: Partially personalized AI
arms.description: Same personalized prompt, but filled with the profile and interview summary of another participant in the study

participants.exclusions: 461 recruited; 130 excluded: 12 failed at least 1 of 2 attention checks, 65 used an AI tool other than the one provided (e.g., ChatGPT), 42 did not engage with the interview chatbot and the AI task assistant, 11 finished in under 30 minutes. The paper does not say how many were assigned before exclusion; several exclusion reasons concern behavior during the task, so the 331 is a post-exclusion sample, not intention-to-treat. The paper's arm counts (116/114/101) are called 'randomized' but are post-exclusion counts.
participants.who: Prolific workers with self-reported work experience in design/creative, marketing, or product management; mean age 38.7; 49.8% female; 73.1% with at least a bachelor's degree; 31.1% marketing experts, 34.1% product experts, 34.7% neither
participants.quote: Of the 461 participants recruited, 12 were excluded ... After applying these exclusion criteria, a sample of 331 individuals was brought forward for analysis with 116 participants randomized to generic AI, 114 to personalized AI, and 101 to partially personalized AI
participants.locator: p. 18-19, Materials and Methods: Participants; PDF p. 52 (suppl. p. 24), Table S2

ai_tool.how_used: Participants chatted freely with the assistant while writing the campaign (mean 5.8 messages, SD 4.5, range 1-20); no guidance on how to use it. The assistant was prompted to ask questions, build on contributions, and deliver the final 300-400-word brief when requested. The personalized versions differ only by the inserted profile and interview summary.

task.description: Write a 300-400-word marketing campaign for 'Cultivated', a fictional lab-grown ribeye startup, covering five components (positioning, target audience, messaging and trust building, channel strategy, success metrics); an initial campaign idea was provided as optional starting point. Could also be read as idea_generation (business/marketing plan).
task.duration: Whole study about 45 minutes; at least 5 minutes requested on the task; mean time on task 18.9 minutes (SD 14.7) (p. 21)

outcomes.name: Campaign quality, LLM judge (GPT-4o-mini, rubric score 1-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o-mini (temperature 0) rates overall quality and likely effectiveness 1-10 using a rubric on strategic soundness and positioning, messaging and trust building, and tactical plan and feasibility (rubric asks to 'Focus on strategic depth, creativity, feasibility, and persuasiveness'). OLS with turn count as control. Robustness variants: average of 4 small LLM judges, Personalized 0.35 (0.16), Partial 0.34 (0.16); average of 3 large LLM judges, Personalized 0.36 (0.18), Partial 0.26 (0.17) (Table S3); modified evaluation criteria 0.50 (0.19) and 0.44 (0.19); simplified criteria (1-5 Likert) 0.10 (0.07) and 0.10 (0.07), not significant (Table S4); LLM pairwise Elo: Personalized beta = 79.7, SE = 35.4, p = 0.02 (Fig. S2B caption; text on p. 7 and suppl. p. 4 says p = 0.03), Partial 38.6, SE = 34.4, p = 0.26. Placebo prompts (different company, unrelated task) show no effect. Model with skills interaction (Fig. 2A): Personalized beta = 2.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.03; Partial beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.21.

contrasts.reported: Personalized 0.59 (0.21)** vs reference Generic, OLS controlling for turn count (Table S3, GPT 4o-mini column); text: beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21, p = 0.005. With skills interaction: beta = 2.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.03 (Fig. 2A).
contrasts.locator: p. 6, Results; PDF p. 59 (suppl. p. 31), Table S3; p. 9, Fig. 2A

contrasts.reported: Partial Personalization 0.56 (0.21)** (Table S3, GPT 4o-mini column); in the model with skills interaction beta = 1.4, SE = 1.1, p = 0.21 ('we find no difference with the partially personalized AI', p. 7).
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 59 (suppl. p. 31), Table S3; p. 7 and p. 9, Fig. 2A

outcomes.name: Campaign quality, human expert pairwise Elo (validation subsample)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: 200 U.S. Prolific raters in upper or middle management, consulting, or market research each made 10 pairwise judgments ('Which campaign has better overall quality?') on a random subset of 100 campaigns from the generic and personalized arms only; each campaign rated 39.6 times on average (range 26-55); Elo ratings (start 1500, K = 32). Correlation with LLM Elo r = 0.72.

contrasts.reported: 'no significant difference between treatment conditions (beta = 158.2, p = 0.14), although the results are directionally correct'; arm split of the 100 campaigns not stated.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 32 (suppl. p. 4), Methods: Sensitivity Analyses

outcomes.name: Campaign creativity (embedding distance of the campaign's themes from the average campaign)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: GPT-4o extracts 1-3-word distinctive themes from each campaign (positioning, audience, messaging, channels, emotional triggers); themes embedded with OpenAI text-embedding-3-large; creativity defined from 'the cosine similarity between its unique themes and the average text embedding of all campaigns across treatment conditions'. Higher score = less similar to the average campaign (p. 10: 'lower scores indicate less creative and more homogenous campaigns'). The rescaling that yields scores near 30-60 is not stated. The paper frames this as homogenization, but the centroid is pooled over all conditions, so the score is per-campaign rarity rather than within-arm dispersion. Robustness variant: creativity by LLM Elo quality tertile (Fig. S2C).

contrasts.reported: All campaigns: personalized Creativity_mean = 52.3, 95% CI [46.8, 57.8] vs generic 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2] (no test reported for this overall contrast).
contrasts.locator: p. 10, 'Personalization as Pathway to Counteract AI-Based Homogenization'

contrasts.reported: All campaigns: partially personalized Creativity_mean = 56.5, 95% CI [51.0, 62.1] vs generic 53.7, 95% CI [48.2, 59.2] (no test reported for this overall contrast).

Subgroup: highest quality tertile (LLM score 8/10) only: beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5, p = 0.002 (Fig. 2B). By LLM Elo top third: beta = 17.6, SE = 5.5, p = 0.002 (Fig. S2C). Subgroup is defined by a post-treatment outcome; n in tertile not stated. Low and medium tertiles shown only in the figure.
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Fig. 2B caption; p. 10; PDF pp. 53-54 (suppl. pp. 25-26), Fig. S2C

contrasts.reported: Subgroup: highest quality tertile only: beta = 15.5, SE = 6.6, p = 0.02 (Fig. 2B). By LLM Elo top third: beta = 17.1, SE = 6.5, p = 0.01 (Fig. S2C).
contrasts.locator: p. 9, Fig. 2B caption; PDF p. 54 (suppl. p. 26), Fig. S2C

outcomes.name: Campaign creativity, AI-only vs human-AI
outcomes.question: none
outcomes.measure_detail: Same embedding creativity score as S1-O3. Quality of AI-only campaigns: 'all 100 campaigns are high quality, i.e., scoring 8/10' (p. 10; Fig. 2B caption) but 'approximately 80% of AI only campaigns are of high quality' (Fig. S2C caption).

company_involvement.description: All authors at Northeastern University; 'Authors declare that they have no competing interests.' Funding section is empty.

data_and_code.data_url: OSF repository 'CreativityBot: A Personalized AI Assistant to Support Creativity' (named on p. 19 and p. 28; no URL printed)

eligibility.reason: S1 randomly assigned individuals to three generative-AI configurations (ai_design; there is no no-AI arm, p. 21). 331 people analyzed after excluding 130 of 461 recruited. Creativity (embedding score) and quality (LLM judge; human expert Elo on a subset) are scored on the campaigns. S2 (AI-only campaigns) is ai_vs_human context only.

one_line_finding: Among 331 Prolific workers, a personalized GPT-4o assistant raised LLM-judged campaign quality relative to a generic one (beta = 0.59, SE = 0.21; p. 6, Table S3), but mean embedding creativity did not differ across arms (52.3 [46.8, 57.8] personalized vs 53.7 [48.2, 59.2] generic; p. 10), with higher creativity only within the top quality tertile (beta = 20.5, SE = 6.5; Fig. 2B).
open_questions: Should the embedding creativity score (S1-O3) be coded as novelty (with_ai) or as diversity (across_people)? It measures each campaign's distance from the centroid of all campaigns pooled across arms; the paper calls it creativity and also reads it as homogeneity.
The creativity effects the paper highlights are within the top quality tertile, a subgroup defined by a post-treatment outcome; the full-sample arm means show no clear difference.

The paper says 're-registered' (p. 19); the registration content (primary outcome, arms) is not printed in the document. candidates.json notes that the OSF registration planned a no-AI condition, which this paper does not report; unverified here.
Exclusions include 65 people who used another AI tool and 42 who did not engage with the assistant, which may differ by arm; the number assigned per arm before exclusion is not reported.

Inconsistencies: LLM Elo personalization p = 0.03 (p. 7, suppl. p. 4) vs p = 0.02 (Fig. S2B); AI-only campaigns 'all' high quality (p. 10) vs 'approximately 80%' (Fig. S2C); interaction beta = -0.23 in text vs '< -0.10' in Fig. 2A panel label.
notes: Self-reported outcomes (trust, confidence, recommendation, feedback, assistance, cognitive support) and conversation-process outcomes (act/coordinate turns, mediation) are not scored on the output and are not listed. Quality is coded as usefulness because the rubric rates overall quality and effectiveness; it explicitly includes creativity among its criteria. Each participant produced one campaign, so output-level and participant-level units coincide in S1. PDF page = printed main-text page; supplement page k = PDF page 28 + k.
